content: DAFx-16 'Rounding Corners with BLAMP' (Esqueda/Valimaki/Bilbao) Table 1 gives the FOUR-point polyBLAMP residual as quintic in d: d^5/120; -d^5/40+d^4/24+d^3/12+d^2/12+d/24+1/120; d^5/40-d^4/12+d^2/3-d/2+7/30; -d^5/120+d^4/24-d^3/12+d^2/12-d/24+1/120. The paper states 'A two-point version of the polyBLAMP function can be found in [21]' but focuses solely on the four-point method. The two-point polyBLAMP residual is therefore CUBIC (integrate the 2-point/linear-B-spline polyBLEP once more): (1-d)^3/6 at the sample before the corner, d^3/6 at the sample after. Residual is scaled by the magnitude and direction of the first-derivative discontinuity. Table 2: four-point polyBLAMP on a trivial triangular C8 gives 46 dB SNR vs 30 dB trivial and 45 dB for 4x oversampling - i.e. ~45 dB is the realistic ceiling for polynomial BLAMP at C8, not 60 dB.
